title: Dynamic (inertial, time-stepped) DEM floe breakage: kernel K(d,d'), energy ledger, FSD power law

delta_vs_p233w1_n04.w1_instrument: quasi-static displacement-controlled lattice fracture (no inertia, no absolute rate, energy ledger is an identity U(before)-U(after))
delta_vs_p233w1_n04.w2_instrument: explicit central-difference dynamics of the same bonded lattice: rigid-wall impact loading, real time axis, kinetic energy in the ledger, breakage hazard measured as events per unit TIME (1/s) instead of per unit applied strain
delta_vs_p233w1_n04.w1_verdict: AC2 FAIL: differential alpha = 3.415 outside [2.0,3.0]; W1 note flagged that pure-breakage PBE has no steady state
delta_vs_p233w1_n04.w2_question: with the dynamic kernel, does the same population balance reach a power-law steady state and where does the exponent sit?

acceptance_criteria.AC1: kernel calibration: daughter-distribution summary fitted on the calibration half predicts the held-out half (held-out = own lattice sizes and impact velocities) with residual <= 10%
acceptance_criteria.AC2: power-law steady state at t = 1000 s: alpha in [2.0, 3.0] with log-linear R^2 >= 0.95
acceptance_criteria.AC3: breakage energy ledger: |E0 - (KE + U_elastic + U_wall + E_dissipated + E_fracture)| / E0 <= 10%
acceptance_criteria.AC4: mass conservation: bond breaking conserves node mass, so fragment area sum residual <= 1e-6, and the population balance area moment drift <= 1e-6
acceptance_criteria.AC5: time-step convergence: DEM runs at dt and dt/2 give |delta alpha| < 0.1
acceptance_criteria.AC6: paper-quality report with FSD evolution and power-law figures

conventions_fixed_in_advance.conserved_measure: floe area A ~ d^2 (constant floe thickness), so daughter normalisation is sum x_i^2 = 1
conventions_fixed_in_advance.alpha_convention: alpha_differential = slope of log10 n(d) vs log10 d; alpha_cumulative = alpha_differential - 1. Observation window [-3,-2] is quoted for the CUMULATIVE (N(>d)) convention; the differential window is then [2,3]. Both are reported, no convention switching after the fact.
conventions_fixed_in_advance.scaling_range: sections strictly inside [d_min*2, d_max/2] on a 2-per-octave area grid, only sections with n > 0
conventions_fixed_in_advance.sink_law: lateral melt: floe diameter shrinks at a constant lateral melt velocity, so the first-order removal rate is mu(d) = 2*v_lat/d, i.e. exponent p = 1 in mu = mu_ref (d/d_ref)^-p. p is taken from the perimeter/area geometry (independent science, Maykut & Perovich 1987 lateral melt 1e-6..1e-5 m/s), NOT tuned to land in the window. mu_ref reported; sensitivity to mu_ref is reported as a curve.
conventions_fixed_in_advance.source_law: level-ice calving into the largest 1-2 sections at a fixed area injection rate
conventions_fixed_in_advance.no_post_hoc_windows: if alpha misses the window the node reports honest FAIL; the sink exponent may not be re-fitted to the fitted alpha

falsifiable_predictions.P1: flux-balance scaling law: alpha_differential = 1 + q + r, where q is the measured breakage-rate exponent nu(d) ~ d^q and r is the measured exponent of the cumulative daughter count C(x) = E[#daughters smaller than x*d'] ~ x^r. The law is tested, not assumed.
falsifiable_predictions.P2: energy-size law: specific breakage energy (threshold impact kinetic energy per floe mass) follows a power of d; exponents 0.5 (Bond, E ~ d^2.5 with mass ~ d^2), 0.0 (Kick) and -1.0 (Rittinger, E ~ new surface ~ d) are the three classical candidates and are compared against the measurement.
